summary: Chijo Akamatsu (1886–1960) was a religious studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo under Bunzaburo Matsumoto. His posts included Keijo Imperial University (1927–1941), Ryukoku University, Hanazono University, Kyoto University, Kyushu University, and Yamaguchi University.
Chijun Hamada is a scholar in Buddhist studies who was attested in 1978 as an assistant at Taisho University and as a researcher at its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute.

Chikafumi Watanabe is a Buddhist studies scholar. He earned a master's at the University of British Columbia and a PhD at the University of Calgary, studying under Leslie S. Kawamura, Ashok Aklujkar, Karin Preisendanz, and others.
Chiken Kato (1943–2017) was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University and served as a professor at Tokyo Polytechnic University (attested 2006).
Chiko Corona is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under traditional teachers Kenko Yamashita and Shohaku Okumura (attested 2010).
Chikyo Yamamoto (1910–1988) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held appointments at Koyasan University as a professor (attested 1970) and part-time lecturer (attested 1980).
Chime Rinpoche (1941–2026) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Gangshar circa 1957–1959 and held a post at the British Library.

Chin Kung (1927–2022) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who studied under Dongmei Fang, Lee Ping-nan, and the 7th Changkya Khutukhtu. He held posts at Chinese Culture University and Pure Land Learning College.

Ching Keng is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, also studying at UT Austin, and became an associate professor at National Chengchi University around 2011.

Ching-mei Shyu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi under Jan Nattier and completed her PhD in 2008 at Cornell University under Daniel Boucher and Hubert Durt.
Chirapat Prapandvidya (born 1941) is an Indology scholar who founded Silpakorn University, served as its director, and taught Kazuhiro Yamamoto.

Chisan Kohō (1879–1967) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and Kyōdō Kōshūin, and founded Tsurumi University in 1966. He held posts at Saijō-ji, Nagano Ken Senmon Nisodo, and Soji-ji (circa 1957–1967).
Chishō Namai (born 1945) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served at Koyasan University as a professor (attested 1996) and president (attested 2008).

Chitai Takenaka (born 1945) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (graduating in 1968) and held posts at Hanazono University (attested 1979–1983) and Tokoha Gakuen University (attested 1989).
Chiyong Kim is a Buddhist studies scholar who held professorships at International Buddhist University and Shitennoji Junior College (both attested 1976).

Chizen Akanuma (1884–1937) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University, Kōkōdō, and under Vagirajnana Jnanissara and Manshi Kiyozawa. He co-founded the Eastern Buddhist Society (1921) and served as a professor at Otani University.

Chizuko Yoshimizu (born 1959) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. She studied at Gakushuin University, University of Tokyo, and University of Vienna (PhD 1994). She held posts at Naritasan Institute, University of Tsukuba, and Toyo Bunko.
Chlodwig H. Werba is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held academic posts at the University of Vienna (attested 1997–2006 and 2022).
Chogye Shabdrung (born 1981) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sakya College in 2003 and was taught by Sonam Gyatso.
Chogye Trichen (1920–2007) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Thubten Gyatso. He served as the Eighteenth Chogye Trichen at Nalendra Monastery from circa 1932 to 2007.
